item.title: Wesele takes charge

item.content:encoded:
FORMER Fiji Bati player Jone Wesele has been handed the task of leading the Vodafone Fiji Bulikula after being appointed head coach yesterday.

Fiji National Rugby League (FNRL) chairman Rajesh Singh announced Wesele’s appointment at FNRL House, with the former international now preparing to take charge of the national women’s side for the biggest assignment of his coaching career. With less than 50 days before the Rugby League World Cup, Wesele knows the preparation window is short, but believes the team can make the most of the time available.

“It’s really humbling to take on the baton from my predecessor,” Wesele said. Rather than making major changes, Wesele intends to build on the work already done by the previous coaching staff and work closely with the existing coaching team.

His immediate priority is bringing the local and overseas-based players together, with unity forming the foundation of his coaching philosophy. “One thing is unity,” Wesele said.

“If everyone comes together as a group, I believe nothing is impossible.”

The former Bati has also set his sights on improving Fiji’s position among the leading women’s rugby league nations, believing the Bulikula can move up the world rankings following the tournament. But Wesele’s ultimate ambition is much bigger.

“I’m ready to take on the challenge … and work towards the same goal, and that is to achieve the World Cup dream, and that is to win,” he said.

Beyond the World Cup, Wesele believes the future of the Bulikula depends on developing a stronger domestic pathway for women’s rugby league.

He wants more competitions for girls at primary and secondary school level, as well as through communities and clubs, giving players more opportunities to gain valuable match experience.

“Game fitness is different from fitness itself,” he said.

Wesele said regular competition would help players develop their knowledge, understanding and confidence before making the step up to international rugby league.

The Bulikula will now prepare for a historic World Cup campaign after securing qualification by winning the World Series qualifier, defeating Nigeria 62–4 in the final. Fiji has been drawn in Pool B alongside New Zealand, Papua New Guinea and France.

The Bulikula will face New Zealand on October 18, Papua New Guinea on October 24 and France on October 31. With a challenging pool ahead and little time to prepare, Wesele begins his tenure with a clear objective, unite the squad, build on the existing foundation and chase Fiji’s World Cup dream.

item.title: ACS battle through to semis semifinals
item.description: ADI Cakobau School (ACS) produced a composed performance on day two of the 2026 Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Basketball Championship, edging St Joseph’s Secondary School 20–16 to secure a place in today’s under-19 semifinals. The defending champions were pushed throughout the final pool match, but ACS held its ground against a determined St Joseph’s outfit to finish the day with a crucial victo
item.content:encoded:
ADI Cakobau School (ACS) produced a composed performance on day two of the 2026 Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Basketball Championship, edging St Joseph’s Secondary School 20–16 to secure a place in today’s under-19 semifinals.

The defending champions were pushed throughout the final pool match, but ACS held its ground against a determined St Joseph’s outfit to finish the day with a crucial victory.

The four-point result keeps ACS firmly in the hunt for another championship, with the semifinal stage now providing the next test in their title defence.

ACS coach Anna Rose was pleased with the way her players handled the pressure of the contest.

“It wasn’t an easy game, it was a tough game against St. Joseph, but I’m really glad the girls did it. I’m very proud of them,” Rose said.

For Rose, the result was a reward for the team’s commitment to training and discipline throughout the tournament.

“It’s just all about training and listening, discipline, most importantly it’s just discipline,” she said.

With the semifinals scheduled for today, Rose said the team would use the short turnaround to recover and identify areas that need improvement from yesterday’s match.

“Maybe we’ll try and improve on our game today. If there’s any mistakes that we’ve done, we are witnesses and we’ll try and work it out again tomorrow,” she said.

The coach said the players must now take responsibility when they step onto the court.

“Everything they’ll do tomorrow will be based on them,” she said.

“Because we’re not the ones playing inside the court, it’s just them.”

Rose brings her own experience of the ACS program into the campaign, having been part of last year’s team that won the U19 title. She is now helping guide the current squad as they attempt to retain the crown.

She also acknowledged the support from ACS Old Girls, teachers and parents who have backed the team throughout the championship.

ACS will now move into the knockout stage, with the U19 semifinals to be played today at the Vodafone Arena, where they will look to turn yesterday’s hard-fought win into another step towards defending their title.

item.title: Royal honours for Nand and Compain
item.description: SANDRA Compain and Ashwin Nand made history last Saturday after being crowned the inaugural Hibiscus Golf Queen and King at the FGC Hibiscus King and Queen Golf Classic at the Fiji Golf Club in Suva. The new tournament attracted 115 golfers who took to the course despite windy and wet conditions, adding a new sporting feature to the 70th anniversary celebrations of the Hibiscus Festival.
item.content:encoded:
SANDRA Compain and Ashwin Nand made history last Saturday after being crowned the inaugural Hibiscus Golf Queen and King at the FGC Hibiscus King and Queen Golf Classic at the Fiji Golf Club in Suva.

The new tournament attracted 115 golfers who took to the course despite windy and wet conditions, adding a new sporting feature to the 70th anniversary celebrations of the Hibiscus Festival.

Compain claimed the women’s title while Nand secured the men’s crown after recording the highest overall points in their respective divisions.

The tournament was initiated by the Suva City Council Hibiscus Committee and SCC Special Administrator Jone Gonewai, with organisers hoping the event will become an annual fixture during the festival.

Tournament chairman Alex Konrote said the inaugural event was a fitting way to celebrate the milestone anniversary.

“Again another glorious day of golf and what a way to celebrate 70 years of the Hibiscus Festival with a golf tournament in one of the Pacific’s oldest Golf Courses right here in the capital city,” Konrote said.

The tournament also brought together the 12 Hibiscus contestants, who took part in the prize presentations, while Speaker of Parliament and Fiji Golf Club patron Filimone Jitoko and Minister for Immigration Viliame Naupoto were among the golfers.

Tomasi Tuivuna claimed the Professional Winner title with 34 points, while junior golfer Christian Qiolevu produced the standout score of the tournament’s junior division, finishing as overall champion with 51 points.

Seresio Colailago won the A Grade with 40 points, Gyanesh Reuben topped B Grade with 39, and Christopher Surendra took C Grade with 38.

Sunita Matthews won the Ladies Overall category with 35 points.

Qiolevu’s 51 points saw him finish ahead of Ethan Qiokevu on 47 and Isireli Digitaki on 40 in the junior division.

Lusi Leqa and Eroni Madanawa claimed the women’s and men’s Longest Drive honours, while Seini Loga and Niu Tabanakaiwai were recognised for Best Dressed.

The inaugural Hibiscus Golf Classic provided a competitive day of golf while introducing a new sporting tradition to Suva’s 70th Hibiscus Festival celebrations.

item.title: Wainibuka claims crown defying all odds
item.description: WAINIBUKA Secondary School’s under-19 girls’ volleyball team defied the odds to claim the Central Eastern Secondary Schools Volleyball Championship title after defeating Kadavu Provincial Secondary School two sets to one in the final. The Wainibuka girls entered the competition without proper facilities to train and with little expectation of making it to the final.
item.content:encoded:
WAINIBUKA Secondary School’s under-19 girls’ volleyball team defied the odds to claim the Central Eastern Secondary Schools Volleyball Championship title after defeating Kadavu Provincial Secondary School two sets to one in the final.

The Wainibuka girls entered the competition without proper facilities to train and with little expectation of making it to the final.

Captain Penina Ranadi said the team had faced several difficulties but remained determined to give their best.

“We faced a lot of difficulties when we came here, but we never gave up,” Ranadi said.

She said the players did not expect their campaign to take them all the way to the final.

“We didn’t dream of reaching the finals, and yet we did. We went on to win the U19 title.”

The team’s preparation was also affected by the lack of proper facilities, but Ranadi said the players made the most of what was available to them.

“We didn’t have proper facilities to train, but we still came out here and gave it our best.”

Their determination paid off when they overcame Kadavu Provincial Secondary School in a closely fought three-set final to secure the championship.

Ranadi said winning the title was a special achievement for the team, considering the challenges they had overcome.

“It means a lot to us because we came here facing difficulties, and we didn’t expect to reach this far.”

She also expressed her gratitude to the parents and supporters who stood behind the team throughout the competition.

“We are very grateful to our parents and all our supporters for supporting us throughout this journey.”

In other results Gospel High School won the U19 boys title defeating William Cross College two straight sets, the U17 boys Nasinu Secondary School won the title defeating Gospel High School two straight sets and in the U17 girls Mahatma Ghandi Memorial School won the title after defeating Ballantine Memorial School two straight sets at the netball centre in Suva.

item.title: Fresh approach urged for World Cup
item.description: FORMER Fiji Rugby Union director Franck Boivert has applied for the Flying Fijians head coach position, outlining an ambitious plan aimed at transforming Fiji’s approach ahead of the next Rugby World Cup. Boivert said Fiji needed a clear and effective game plan if it was to have a realistic chance at the Rugby World Cup.
item.content:encoded:
FORMER Fiji Rugby Union director Franck Boivert has applied for the Flying Fijians head coach position, outlining an ambitious plan aimed at transforming Fiji’s approach ahead of the next Rugby World Cup.

Boivert said Fiji needed a clear and effective game plan if it was to have a realistic chance at the Rugby World Cup.

Boivert, who has extensive experience in Fiji rugby development, was highly critical of aspects of Fiji’s approach during the last World Cup campaign, particularly the team’s preparation, tactical execution and defensive organisation.

He said his first priority, if appointed, would be to address Fiji’s struggles against driving mauls and improve the players’ understanding of their functional roles.

“Conceding three tries on that phase versus Wales is absolutely unacceptable,” Boivert said, adding that he would introduce specific systems to ensure the forwards were organised before an opposition maul was established.

He also wants greater emphasis placed on decision-making, adaptability and communication at training.

Boivert said training should involve opposition and game-based situations rather than relying heavily on repetitive drills.

“The players must constantly adapt to the situation,” he said.

He also outlined plans to develop Fiji’s counter-attacking ability, attack immediately off the advantage line and create more freedom for players to attack from different areas of the field.

Boivert said he would look closely at the workload of Fiji’s overseas-based players, particularly those competing in the demanding Top 14 season, and would seek to manage their preparation carefully.

He identified France-based fullback Seta Tuicuvu as a player he would select, saying he believed Tuicuvu could make a major impact at the World Cup.

“I know for a fact that Jiuta Wainiqolo and Seta Tuicuvu will perform fantastic at the World Cup,” he said.

Boivert ended his submission with a light-hearted reminder of his previous application, saying: “I hope FRU don’t lose my letter this time.”

item.title: Drua connection boosts Fijiana
item.description: THE strong presence of McDonald’s Fiji Drua Women players in the Vodafone Fijiana XV squad is providing the side with an important foundation as it prepares for its Test against Japan on September 4. Fijiana XV head coach Willie Walker said the relationships already developed among the Drua players have helped the national side build combinations as it prepares for the one-off Test and the WXV Glo
item.content:encoded:
THE strong presence of McDonald’s Fiji Drua Women players in the Vodafone Fijiana XV squad is providing the side with an important foundation as it prepares for its Test against Japan on September 4.

Fijiana XV head coach Willie Walker said the relationships already developed among the Drua players have helped the national side build combinations as it prepares for the one-off Test and the WXV Global Series Challenger in Hong Kong.

The Challenger tournament will run from September 13 to 26.

Walker said one of the major benefits of having several Drua players in the Fijiana XV squad was their understanding of each other’s game.

“They understand each other. They already have those relationships,” Walker said.

“They understand how each player plays the game, so that connection is automatically there.”

However, Walker said the transition into the national team environment has also required the players to adapt because the Fijiana XV is introducing systems and approaches different from those used by the Drua.

The coaching staff is also working to integrate players who were not part of the Drua squad and ensure everyone understands their roles.

Walker believes the senior players in the squad will play an important role in that process.

He said experienced players who have already played Test rugby understand the standards and expectations required at international level.

“The senior players are vital in making sure that our new players that are coming into this environment understand what it means to be here, firstly, to play for Fijiana,” Walker said.

Walker also reminded the players that earning a place in the Fijiana XV squad is only the beginning of their international journey.

He expects every player to continue challenging themselves and improving each day.

The coach said the long-term growth of the programme depended on creating an environment where players were prepared to work harder to retain their positions.

item.title: Ritova grateful for journey
item.description: RATU Kadavulevu School (RKS) captain and point guard Opeti Ritova says he is grateful for the journey his team experienced at the 2026 Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Basketball Championship, held yesterday at the Vodafone Arena. RKS’ campaign came to an end after they were beaten 16–12 by Natabua High School in their final pool match.
item.content:encoded:
RATU Kadavulevu School (RKS) captain and point guard Opeti Ritova says he is grateful for the journey his team experienced at the 2026 Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Basketball Championship, held yesterday at the Vodafone Arena.

RKS’ campaign came to an end after they were beaten 16–12 by Natabua High School in their final pool match.

Despite the disappointment of the defeat, Ritova reflected positively on the team’s efforts and the commitment they showed throughout their preparation for the championship.

“I want to thank God, for the journey where we would run up the hills for training,” Ritova said.

For the RKS captain, the opportunity to compete at the national secondary schools championship was the result of the hard work put in by the players leading into the tournament.

“I believe it was God’s calling for us to reach the pool game and make it this far,” he said.

As captain and point guard, Ritova carried an important responsibility on the court, helping organise the team and guide his teammates during their matches.

Although RKS fell short against Natabua, the four-point margin reflected a competitive final pool game, with both teams battling for an important result.

The experience also gave the RKS players an opportunity to test their skills against other schools and gain valuable exposure at the national level.

item.title: Seru rues missed opportunities
item.description: THE McDonald’s Nadi Women’s captain Laisa Seru has expressed disappointment after her side was held to a 22-all draw by Macuata Women in a thrilling Round Five encounter of the Subrails Marama Cup Competition at Churchill Park in Lautoka yesterday. The result saw both sides share the spoils after an intense battle, but Seru believed Nadi had opportunities to secure the win.
item.content:encoded:
THE McDonald’s Nadi Women’s captain Laisa Seru has expressed disappointment after her side was held to a 22-all draw by Macuata Women in a thrilling Round Five encounter of the Subrails Marama Cup Competition at Churchill Park in Lautoka yesterday.

The result saw both sides share the spoils after an intense battle, but Seru believed Nadi had opportunities to secure the win.

“It was a very disappointing game. We could have done better than that and I thought we were a bit too casual with our hands in our 22-metre mark that allowed Macuata some tries,” Seru said.

Seru said Nadi had expected a tough contest, particularly given Macuata’s strong form coming into the match.

“We knew Macuata was going to come out stronger against us considering they came back with back-to-back wins in the last two weeks,” she said.

Despite the missed opportunities, Seru praised her teammates for showing resilience and refusing to surrender the match.

She said the draw reflected the team’s determination to hold their ground when Macuata applied pressure, especially during the crucial stages of the encounter.

Seru revealed that the match also carried special significance for the Nadi women, who dedicated their performance to the memory of one of the club’s founding figures, Seini Koop, who passed away a few days ago.

The loss had an emotional impact on the players, with Seru acknowledging that the team was still mourning the passing of a person who had played an important role in the development of women’s rugby in Nadi.

“I am so glad the girls did their all today,” Seru said.

“We lost one of our club founders a few days ago. We are mourning the loss of Mrs Seini Koop, and I think that played a bigger part in the morale of the girls today.

“But I am grateful the girls did not give away too much of the game. We held our fort and came away with a draw with Macuata.”

The Nadi captain will now look for her side to learn from the mistakes and return stronger in their next match.
